text:
Maya: Quick alignment thread 174: need final GA commitments: SLAs, pricing mechanics, docs minimum, and oncall handoffs. Aim to ship defaults this week.

Sanjay: I'll take the SLA text. Draft idea: measurement = rolling 30d window (not calendar) to reduce month-boundary noise. Levels: Hosted: 99.8 availability, Dedicated: 99.95, Private: SLA only if we manage infra. Will draft credit calc.

Aaron: Why 99.8 for hosted? Feels low compared to market.

Sanjay: Tradeoff: we want realistic SLOs given multi-tenant bursty workloads and our early autoscaler behavior. We can offer 99.95 as a paid premium add-on for hosted with reserved throughput.

Zoe: Pricing implications: if hosted baseline is 99.8, capacity buffer required is lower but customers may complain. Proposed billing model: blended subscription + usage. Hosted default = metered tokens, plus optional "priority lane" subscription for 99.95 that includes reserved qps. Burst handling: soft cap window (3m). Soft exceed -> billed at 1.8x; sustained exceed beyond 15m -> either escalate to capacity or throttle (customer choice at signup).

Ellie: Docs must include a tiny SLA FAQ and a one-page "What triggers a credit" with examples. Also add a short tutorial: "simulate your workload" (curl snippet + load pattern) so customers can validate hitting soft caps. I can draft by Wed.

Rafael: Oncall: Hosted incidents -> infra-platform rotation first; Priority-lane (paid) incidents -> dedicated oncall + platform. Dedicated customers get their own oncall contact in contract. Private -> SE + customer ops. We'll need to publish contact matrix in the docs.

Maya: Good. Sanjay, include measurement method (rolling 30d), credit formula, and exclusions (DDoS, customer infra, third-party networks). Also specify SLA reporting cadence (monthly report and automated PDF on request).

Sanjay: Credit formula idea: credit% = min(30, floor((1 - availability) * 1000)). Example: 99.8 => 0.2% downtime -> credit = floor(0.2*1000)=200 -> cap to 30 => 30%? That seems weird. Maybe use tiers: <99.5 = 25% credit, 99.5-99.9 = 10%, >99.9 = 5%. Feedback?

Aaron: That formula looks odd. Keep it simple: tiered credits: outage <12h -> 5%, 12-72h -> 15%, >72h -> 30%, applied to monthly invoice prorated by affected service. Simpler and defensible.

Sanjay: Agreed. Using time buckets is clearer. I'll update.

Zoe: Billing edge cases: trial accounts get a conservative soft-burst cap (e.g., 100k tokens/day). If exceeded, we'll email and throttle rather than charge automatically. GA docs should call this out.

Ellie: Also add a short "billing dispute" flow: timeline for submitting claims (30 days), required evidence (request IDs + timestamps), and expected resolution SLA (10 business days).

Rafael: Monitoring: propose core GA alerts: p95 latency (token), p99 tail latency > 0.9s for 5m, error rate > 0.8% for 10m, and system CPU/GPU saturation > 85% for 5m. Pages if p99 or error conditions occur.

Maya: Include labels on alerts for model_id, deployment_type, customer_tier. Also include a note for cache_hit label to prioritize caching issues.

Rafael: Example alert rule (PromQL):
```
alert: TokenTailLatencyHigh
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_id)) > 0.9
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: "runbooks/alerts/high-tail-latency"
```

Ellie: Runbook will have triage steps: 1) check model_id label, 2) check cache_hit, 3) verify autoscaler events, 4) failover guidance. I'll stub that.

Sanjay: Runtime fallback policy for GA: if a partition drops below 50% available mem or node-count, system will attempt automatic fallback to quantized variant if registered, else mark non-essential routes for degradation. Document opt-out.

Zoe: Need to decide default quantization: 8-bit per-token variant available for fallback? We'll announce supported fallback families in docs.

Maya: Decisions to lock now for GA defaults:
- measurement: rolling 30d (Sanjay)
- hosted baseline: 99.8, optional priority lane 99.95
- credits: tiered time buckets (Aaron)
- burst: soft cap 3m then 1.8x billing, 15m sustained -> throttle/escalate
- oncall matrix per Rafael

Vote: Sanjay?

Sanjay: +1 to the set; will PR SLA text.

Aaron: +1 to credits and dispute flow.

Ellie: +1 to docs scope and runbook skeleton. ETA Wed EOD for drafts.

Rafael: +1, will export alert rules and add runbook TODOs by Tue.

Zoe: +1, will run pricing sims with soft-cap parameters and post results Thu morning.

DeployBot: staging: ga-sla-package v1.0 deployed at 1746667905. Canary tests ongoing. :white_check_mark:

Maya: Thanks all. I'll publish the GA checklist once PRs are in. If anyone wants to dispute the hosted baseline, raise it by EOD Tue with cost/ops tradeoffs. Otherwise we'll roll these as defaults for GA. :pray:
